newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania central bank sacks Columna Bank managers.
newsitem.headline: Romania central bank sacks Columna Bank managers.

text.p: Romania's National Bank (BNR) said on Tuesday it had decided to sack top officials of private bank Columna Bank SA and limit its activities over charges that it repeatedly breached banking rules.
The BNR's Communications Manager, Adrian Vasilescu, said 10 senior officials of Columna, a Swiss-Romanian joint venture, had been dismissed -- managers, board members and founders.

"The BNR has also banned Columna from taking deposits from individuals and corporate clients, both local and foreigners, and restricted its participation in the settlement system," Vasilescu told Reuters.
He said Columna should immediately call a shareholders' meeting to appoint a new board.
The bank's head, Vasile Bostan, resigned last month after the BNR demanded his replacement. He said he wanted to end the bank's conflicts with the BNR and also cited personal reasons.
Columna's main shareholder is Manel Finanz AG, a Swiss financial company which holds about 93 percent of the capital. The remainder is held by Romanian and foreign individuals.

Bostan, also a founder of the bank, is on a BNR list, published in the Official Gazette, of 10 bank managers, administrators and founders banned for five years from holding positions in Romania's banking system.
Vasilescu said Columna bank had been subject to BNR checks on its activities since February. But the central bank stopped short of placing the bank under special surveillance.
"The BNR did not withdraw Columna's banking licence. Columna has not defaulted on payments," Vasilescu said.
